reply_text:
㊢ (written) The ten items are in `futon2/holes/E-aif-cascade.md` as a new section, "Rulings — Joe's items", placed before DERIVE (futon2 `fa6a4a766`). Each has what is being decided, what the record shows with the report it comes from, the options, my recommendation, and a `→ Ruling:` line for you to fill with a word. A table at the end says what each ruling releases, and the re-entry rule now points at the section.

㊭ (the ten, one line each, recommendation in brackets)
R1 the eleven-edge cut of the harness figure [accept as tabled].
R2 the R6 and R4 splits [split R6; treat R4-model as the click's initial have, not a unit].
R3 meet direction, where my two Lean modules disagree [`CascadeOrder`'s: the meet is the common origin; amend `MeetWitness`, re-prove the diamond with `observe` as the meet].
R4 a root unit for the click's input state [add it, so the R-cascade has one root like the outer diamond].
R5 operator load as preference term or support change [preference term].
R6 library coupling recorded or scored [recorded only].
R7 promote `meta/select-the-meta-item` [after B4 part 2 shows one run where its THEN held].
R8 inert tokens as no credit or a cost [no credit now].
R9 where the quality order enters G, c17 vs c10 [c10 for the order, c17's count in ambiguity].
R10 whether Goguen's house/boat order is the order for library patterns [defer, with §2a's reading as the working answer].

㊟ (R9 and R10) I reconstructed the "two v3 decisions" from the draft's §4 and §7 since the earlier report naming them is not in front of me: the route of the quality order into G, and whether Goguen's three criteria are the right order for library patterns. If you had two different ones in mind, say which and I will swap them in.

🈳 (state) codex-33 is idle; nothing dispatchable remains without a ruling. Rulings can come in any order or as one batch, and each releases the items its table row names.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (gist) Added as B1d (futon2 `ff22a2876`), queued for codex-33 right after B1c: a one-line cheat sheet per item, computed from the whole document and its history rather than HEAD. The part of your remark that does the most work for the outer cascade is *register and its direction* — concrete vs abstract, and whether the mission is heading out or coming back — because that is the feasibility signal B2 could not get from commit history (4 of 107 had any), and it is exactly what HEAD alone cannot show.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (the sheet) Five fields, all classical counts so the sheet is the same on every run: *scopes* — repos and directories its paths touch, by count; *keywords* — tf-idf over the 107 plus any declared ones; *the changes* — the applied patterns in order of first mention, the progression under the tune; *register* — per section, the share of lines carrying a path, sha, number, checkbox or date against prose lines, with its trajectory early→late and first commits→last, so "spun off into abstraction" and "returned to something concrete" read as a direction; and the status line. One line: `| scope futon3c/agency ×41 · futon2/aif ×12 | keys clock, lineage, dispatch | changes p1 → p2 → p3 | register 0.62 ↑ |`. Worked examples are your two: `M-weird-modernism` (1,037 lines, 101 paths, 5 checkboxes, "perpetual-projection mode — no closure phase scheduled") and `M-the-perfect-crime` (557 lines, 100 paths, 6 checkboxes, 13 commit shas). Acceptance is that those two read right to you.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (where it enters the cascade) The `observe` square today emits an item as id, kind, source pin and one locator. The sheet is what it should emit instead — the item as a chord chart, not a bar — and register/trajectory become the token the feasibility square consumes, where B2's commit share would have gone. In §5a's terms it is Crumb's panel sequence compressed to a line beside the current panel.
